newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip after Friday's short rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip after Friday's short rise.

text.p: Most leading Russian shares started to edge down on Monday after a strong rise last Friday, as operators finished processing orders from Western investors left over from Friday, traders said.

"Leading shares continued to rise slowly in the morning as they did last Friday, but then started to slip," said Yuri Agaronik of Prospekt. "Probably, last week's buying orders, including Western, have all been met already."

Last Friday the Russian Trading System 21-share index rebounded with a 3.41 percent rise to 171.72 after a week-long fall caused by President Boris Yeltsin's announcement of his future heart operation. The index rises to 24 shares from Monday.
Traders said Friday's advance was due to Western orders spurred by news of progress on rescheduling Russia's debt to its commercial bank creditors and Russian plans to issue Eurobonds.
"Last Friday, we hoped the growth would continue on Monday and expected a fall on Tuesday or Wednesday...But Friday's rally turned out to be too quick," Agaronik said.
At 1030 GMT, Norilsk Nickel was last traded at $6.75 after Friday's close at $6.98. UES fell to $0.0783 from $0.0797. Rostelekom eased to $2.48 from $2.51, and LUKoil fell to $9.35 from $9.45.
Boris Shvedsky of Aton said Russian shares were still more responsive to political news than to economic news and predicted further instability before Yeltsin's operation at the end of this month.
"To my mind, the fall of the stock market will carry on," he said.
